author: Rahul kp
title: Profit Max vs
simple_words: Profit max chases more profit now. Wealth max grows the share's value, counting time and risk.

definitions.meaning: Aim of earning the highest possible accounting profit in the short run, without looking at time or risk.
Aim of increasing the market value of the shareholders' equity, by taking decisions whose present value of benefits exceeds cost.

key_points: Profit max ignores the ==time value of money==: ₹1 today and ₹1 later look equal.
Profit max ignores ==risk==; a risky high profit looks better than a safe lower one.
Wealth max uses cash flows and discounting, so it is the accepted goal in Financial Management.
!!Profit is vague!!: it may mean EBIT, PAT or EPS, so it cannot be measured one way.
formula_hook: learn the table, win the MCQ

insight.punchline: Profit is a number, wealth is value!
insight.text: Wealth maximisation covers timing, risk and all shareholders' returns, which profit maximisation misses.

memory_trick.explanation: Wealth max looks at Time value, Risk and Market price. Profit max looks at none of the three.

steps: Read what the goal looks at
Is time value or risk counted?
No, only profit figure: profit max
Pick the option on market value
exam_tip: If an option says 'maximise market value of equity shares' or 'maximise NPV', it is wealth maximisation.

doubt.question: Does wealth maximisation mean ignoring profit?
doubt.answer: No. Profit still matters, but it is one input. Wealth max judges profit along with timing, risk and cash flows.

mistakes_hook: don't fall for the profit trap

mistakes.wrong: Profit maximisation considers risk and time value
mistakes.right: Profit maximisation ignores both time value of money and risk.

mistakes.wrong: Wealth maximisation means maximising profit of the year
mistakes.right: It means maximising the market value of shareholders' equity over the long run.

mistakes.wrong: Profit is a clear, single measure
mistakes.right: Profit can mean EBIT, PAT or EPS, so the term is ambiguous.

check_notes: Checker 1: Steps 4–5: Step 5 ('Pick the option on market value') comes right after Step 4 concludes 'profit max', so the flow reads badly. Suggested fix: make Step 5 'In MCQs on the goal of FM, choose the option based on market value of shares (wealth max)' or fold it into Step 3.
Checker 1: Insight text: 'all shareholders' returns' is vague. Suggested wording: 'total shareholder returns – dividends plus capital gains (share price)'.
